evidence.detail: Assignment URL has no section; fragment is provider-inventory or provider-package-ID.

Without section or cloud-assignment focus, selected section is overview.
Overview branch omits services controls; services child is included only for that selected section.
Service inventory and package cards do not define either fragment target.
Cloud preparation, refresh and assignment return preserves focus when present, otherwise passes empty query and loses ordinary cloud section.

reproduction_by_source: Open the saved active/confirmed hosting assignment card as the current owner and follow Review client access. The emitted URL lacks section=services. The destination chooses overview and cannot resolve either emitted fragment.
Submit normal cloud refresh or assignment action while in section=cloud without focus=cloud-assignment. After the authorized action, the changed redirect passes no section and selects overview.
findings.impact: Owner loses the intended review/action context and must choose the workspace again. No provider write, access grant, payment, or cross-client exposure is performed by these URLs; no authority bypass is claimed.
correction_invariants: Client-access handoff must explicitly select services and use a fragment that exists on the inventory or exact package card; retain the current owner gate.
Ordinary cloud action returns must select cloud while preserving the existing focused cloud-assignment route when explicitly present.
Navigation must remain fixed local URLs with allowlisted section names; selecting a section must not become provider/assignment authority.

coverage_limits: All 51 previously unreviewed changed clauses are now source-reviewed, but review depths differ and are recorded per path. This is not complete backend certification for every destination.

The shared current-session helper implementation and broader shared administrator/portal routing remain parent-owned; this supplement verifies callers and selected entry gates, not all shared identity internals.
Historical runtime receipts remain historical and bounded; no old test pass is promoted to independent present-day approval. Original core coverage limits and FIN-01/FIN-02 remain unchanged.
Software catalog link routing was reviewed only as a fixed local GET destination. Parent software lane owns SW-AUTH and complete software mutation/entitlement authority review.

Provider operation backends for all nested workspace tools were not re-audited end to end; selected current-owner, exact-binding, lock and unresolved-outcome admission clauses were traced as dependencies.
